name: אֲדֹנִיקָם
summary: The head of a family that came back from Babylon: 666 of his sons returned with Zerubbabel by Ezra’s list (667 by Nehemiah’s), and the last of them, three men named with sixty males, came up with Ezra. The name is אֲדֹנִי “my lord” with קָם, “has arisen, stood up”, a sentence like אֲחִיקָם and עַזְרִיקָם: “my lord has arisen”, as Moses and the psalms call on Yahweh to arise.

evidence.note: “The sons of אֲדֹנִיקָם, six hundred and sixty-six.”
The same family in Nehemiah’s list: six hundred and sixty-seven.
“Of the sons of אֲדֹנִיקָם, the last ones: Eliphelet, Jeiel and Shemaiah, and with them sixty males.”
When the ark set out Moses said קוּמָה יַהְוֶה, “Arise, Yahweh, and let your enemies be scattered”: the verb of the name, said of the Lord.
אֲחִיקָם, “my brother has arisen”: the same pattern.

note: The second element is the verb of entry `qum` (root קומ); a name entry links to one root entry only, so the tie is stated here. עַזְרִיקָם is at 1Ch 3:23.
